newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said 71 percent of the U.S. corn crop was planted versus 50 percent last week, and 52 percent in the same period a year ago.
The five-year average for corn plantings was 50 percent.
In its report on conditions for the week ended May 11, USDA said 20 percent of the soybean crop was planted versus eight percent a year ago and the five-year average of 12 percent.
USDA said five percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, 11 percent in poor, 31 percent fair, 44 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Thirty-three percent of the spring wheat crop was planted compared with 31 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 56 percent.
USDA also said six percent of the spring wheat crop was emerged compared with six percent in the same period last year and the five-year average of 25 percent.

The department also reported 44 percent of the cotton crop was planted, compared with 51 percent in the same period in 1996 and the five-year average of 51 percent. -- Washington Commodities Desk (202) 898-8394
